blocks.text: Prompt sanitization cleans untrusted content before it ever becomes part of a prompt, neutralizing sequences that could break a delimiter structure or stripping obviously suspicious instruction-like phrases, one practical layer of defense against the injection risks covered in the previous two topics.

This topic covers neutralizing delimiter-breaking sequences, handling suspicious instruction-like phrases, when sanitization should actually happen in a pipeline, how it works alongside delimiting, and its real limits as only one layer among several defenses.
1. What Prompt Sanitization Means

blocks.alt: Building on jailbreak attacks, prompt sanitization cleans untrusted content before use

blocks.text: Prompt sanitization is the process of cleaning or transforming untrusted content, before it gets incorporated into a prompt, specifically targeting patterns known to be associated with injection or manipulation attempts.

blocks.alt: Raw untrusted input goes through a sanitization pass, producing cleaned input

blocks.text: 2. Neutralizing Delimiter-Breaking Sequences

blocks.alt: A delimiter breaking sequence gets escaped or neutralized

blocks.text: This connects directly to delimiter-based prompting, covered in an earlier module, if untrusted content happens to contain the exact delimiter sequence a prompt uses to mark boundaries, triple quotes, a specific tag, that content could break out of its intended boundary, sanitization escapes or neutralizes any occurrence of that exact sequence within untrusted content before it gets inserted.

code.content:
def sanitize_for_delimiter(text, delimiter='"""'):
    return text.replace(delimiter, "'''")  # neutralize the exact delimiter sequence

blocks.text: 3. Handling Suspicious Instruction-Like Phrases

blocks.alt: An ignore previous instructions style phrase gets flagged or stripped out

blocks.text: Certain phrase patterns are strongly associated with injection attempts, "ignore previous instructions," "disregard the above," sanitization can flag or strip content containing these known patterns, though this needs to be balanced against the risk of a legitimate document innocently containing similar wording.

blocks.text: 4. When Sanitization Should Happen

blocks.alt: Sanitization happens first, then the prompt gets constructed

blocks.text: Sanitization needs to happen before untrusted content actually gets inserted into a prompt template, covered in an earlier module, sanitizing after the fact, once content is already embedded in a constructed prompt, is far less reliable than cleaning it at the point it first enters the pipeline.
5. Sanitization Works Alongside Delimiting

blocks.alt: Sanitization plus delimiting together form a stronger combined defense

blocks.text: Sanitization and delimiter-based prompting, covered in an earlier module, are complementary, not redundant, delimiting marks where untrusted content begins and ends, sanitization ensures that content itself cannot subvert that marking, using both together provides meaningfully stronger protection than either alone.

blocks.title: Neither technique alone is sufficient
blocks.content: Delimiting without sanitization risks content that breaks out of its own delimiter, sanitization without delimiting still leaves the model without a clear signal about what counts as data versus instruction, the two need to work together.

blocks.text: 6. The Real Limits of Sanitization

blocks.alt: Sanitization cannot catch every novel attack, but it remains one useful layer among several

blocks.text: Sanitization can only catch known, recognized patterns, a genuinely novel injection phrasing that does not match any known pattern will pass through unaffected, this is exactly why sanitization functions as one layer in a defense strategy, not a complete solution on its own.
7. A Worked Sanitization Example

A document processing pipeline sanitizes every retrieved document by neutralizing occurrences of the prompt exact delimiter sequence, and flagging content containing common injection-associated phrases for a stricter review path, before that document ever gets inserted into the actual model prompt.
8. Sanitization for Different Content Types

Sanitization needs vary by content type, plain text content mainly needs delimiter and phrase handling, code content might need additional handling for characters with special meaning in that programming language, structured data like JSON needs its own format specific escaping, matching the specific risks each content type actually carries.
9. Sanitization as One Layer Among Several

This topic sets up the next several topics in this module directly, input validation, output filtering, and guardrails, together with sanitization, form a genuinely layered defense, each catching different classes of problem that sanitization alone would miss.
Worked Example

A team building a document review tool finds their delimiter based prompt structure occasionally breaks when a retrieved document happens to contain the exact triple quote sequence used as their delimiter, allowing document content to appear to the model as if it were outside the intended boundary.

Adding a sanitization step that specifically neutralizes any occurrence of that exact delimiter sequence within retrieved content before insertion resolves this specific vulnerability, while the team continues layering additional defenses, covered in the rest of this module, rather than treating this one fix as complete.
Common Mistakes

items: Sanitizing content after it has already been inserted into a constructed prompt instead of before
Relying on sanitization alone without also using delimiter-based prompting, missing a complementary layer of defense
Assuming sanitization catches every possible injection pattern, including genuinely novel ones it was never designed to recognize
Applying the same sanitization approach to every content type regardless of the specific risks that type actually carries

blocks.text: Practice

Take a prompt template that inserts untrusted content using a specific delimiter, write a sanitization function that neutralizes any occurrence of that exact delimiter within the untrusted content, and test it against content deliberately crafted to contain that delimiter sequence.
Key Takeaway

Prompt sanitization cleans untrusted content before it enters a prompt, neutralizing delimiter-breaking sequences and flagging known injection-associated phrases, working best alongside delimiter-based prompting rather than as a standalone fix, and it remains only one layer among several, unable to catch every genuinely novel attack pattern on its own.
